rounds.text: Despite recent contraction in trailing metrics, Jainam Ferro Alloys (I) Ltd shows fundamental resilience through a modest price-to-book ratio of 1.88x, trading at ₹ 235 on a book value of ₹ 125 [E2]. The company demonstrates operational vitality with a year-over-year sales increase of 8% [E47]. Long-term investors have been rewarded with a 23% compounded share price growth over three years [E10]. Furthermore, the market capitalisation sits at a manageable ₹ 275 Cr [E3], while the stock rests conservatively at 43% of the way up its 52-week range spanning a low of 169 to a high of 323 [E5]. Conceded: the trailing twelve months show a compounded profit growth of -35% alongside an ROCE of 6.9% and an ROE of 4.7% [E6, E7, E9].

Conceded: the company trades at a modest price-to-book ratio of 1.88x on a book value of ₹ 125 [E2], and the share price sits at 43% of its 52-week range [E5]. However, celebrating a year-over-year sales increase of 8% [E47] ignores the trailing twelve-month reality of compounded sales growth contracting by -7% [E8]. While the bull points to a 23% compounded share price growth over 3 years [E10], this outpaces fundamental delivery, as price growth exceeds profit growth by 11%, leaving expectations running ahead of reality [E38]. The manageable market capitalisation of ₹ 275 Cr [E3] provides no comfort when paired with a severe profit contraction of -35% over the trailing twelve months [E9]. Finally, this declining profitability yields a weak ROCE of 6.9% and an ROE of 4.7% [E6, E7], rendering the valuation completely unjustifiable when weighed against fundamental output.
